# ==== Load/memory-read: 68 curated ====
#
# Same rule as sm_75 (Reports/tasks.md Phase 1.1): any InsKey with a destination register is
# VARIABLE:WRITE, including the no-value ATOMS/ATOM "arrive"/"popc.inc" forms (they still write a
# destination, even if it's often RZ) and the new descriptor-addressed (dARI) forms, which are
# just a different way to compute the same address. CCTL/CCTL_ARI have no operand to protect
# (FIXED). RED_dARI_R has no destination, structurally a store (VARIABLE:READ).

ATOMG_P_R_ARI_R: VARIABLE:WRITE  # e.g. "ATOMG.ADD.STRONG.GPU PT, R13, [R0], RZ ;"
ATOMG_P_R_ARI_R_R: VARIABLE:WRITE  # e.g. "ATOMG.E.CAS.STRONG.GPU PT, R11, [R4], R9, R11 ;"
ATOMG_P_R_AURI_R: VARIABLE:WRITE  # e.g. "@P0 ATOMG.ADD.STRONG.GPU PT, R5, [UR4], RZ ;"
ATOMG_P_R_dARI_R: VARIABLE:WRITE  # e.g. "@P0 ATOMG.E.ADD.STRONG.GPU PT, R3, desc[UR8][R2.64+0x8], R7 ;"
ATOMS_R_AI_R: VARIABLE:WRITE  # e.g. "@P1 ATOMS.MIN.S32 RZ, [0x5008], R16 ;"
ATOMS_R_ARI_R: VARIABLE:WRITE  # e.g. "@P1 ATOMS.MAX.S32 RZ, [RZ], R8 ;"
ATOMS_R_ARI_R_R: VARIABLE:WRITE  # e.g. "ATOMS.CAST.SPIN R3, [R0], R2, R3 ;"
ATOMS_R_ARURI: VARIABLE:WRITE  # e.g. "ATOMS.ARRIVE.64 RZ, [R2+URZ+0x8] ;"
ATOMS_R_AURI: VARIABLE:WRITE  # e.g. "ATOMS.POPC.INC.32 RZ, [URZ] ;"
ATOMS_R_AURI_R: VARIABLE:WRITE  # e.g. "@P0 ATOMS.ADD.S32 RZ, [UR12+0x4], R2 ;"
ATOM_P_R_ARI_R: VARIABLE:WRITE  # e.g. "ATOM.ADD.STRONG.GPU PT, R13, [R0], RZ ;"
ATOM_P_R_ARI_R_R: VARIABLE:WRITE  # e.g. "ATOM.E.CAS.STRONG.GPU PT, R0, [R2], R5, R0 ;"
ATOM_P_R_ARURI: VARIABLE:WRITE  # e.g. "ATOM.E.ARRIVE.64.STRONG.SM PT, R4, [R4.U32+URZ] ;"

CCTL: FIXED  # no operand at all to protect with a barrier  # e.g. "CCTL.IVALL ;"

TXQ_R_R_R_L_II_II_II: VARIABLE:WRITE  # e.g. "TXQ RZ, R16, R16, TEX_HEADER_DIMENSION, 0x0, 0x58, 0x2 ;"
TXQ_R_R_R_L_UR_II_II: VARIABLE:WRITE  # e.g. "TXQ RZ, R5, R24, TEX_HEADER_DIMENSION, UR22, 0x0, 0x2 ;"
ULDC_UR_cAI: VARIABLE:WRITE  # e.g. "ULDC UR5, c[0x0][0x0] ;"
ULDC_UR_cAURI: VARIABLE:WRITE  # e.g. "ULDC UR18, c[0x2][UR18+0x24] ;"

# ==== Store: 18 curated ====
#
# All VARIABLE:READ, same reasoning as sm_75 (protects the source value register still being
# consumed asynchronously by the memory write). dARI is just descriptor-based addressing, same
# store shape otherwise. See Reports/tasks.md Phase 1.1.

STL_AURI_R: VARIABLE:READ  # e.g. "STL [UR6], RZ ;"
STS_AI_R: VARIABLE:READ  # e.g. "@!P3 STS [0x5000], R82 ;"
STS_ARI_R: VARIABLE:READ  # e.g. "STS.128 [R0.X16], R4 ;"
STS_ARURI_R: VARIABLE:READ  # e.g. "STS.64 [R96+UR7], R88 ;"
STS_AURI_R: VARIABLE:READ  # e.g. "STS.128 [UR5], R8 ;"

# ==== Control-flow: 37 curated ====
#
# All FIXED, same reasoning as sm_75 (Reports/tasks.md Phase 1.1) -- confirmed empirically there
# for BAR/BMOV/BRA/BSSY/BSYNC/CALL/DEPBAR/EXIT/RET, extended to the rest of this bucket (including
# the new BRA_UR_II indirect-branch form) by direct architectural consistency: none of these write
# a value via the async memory/SFU pipe the 6 scoreboard slots protect.

B2R_R: FIXED  # e.g. "B2R.RESULT R13 ;"
B2R_R_P: FIXED  # e.g. "B2R.RESULT RZ, P0 ;"
BAR_II: FIXED  # e.g. "BAR.SYNC 0x0 ;"
BAR_II_P: FIXED  # e.g. "BAR.RED.AND 0x0, P0 ;"
BAR_R: FIXED  # e.g. "BAR.SYNC R0 ;"
BAR_R_R: FIXED  # e.g. "BAR.SYNC R9, R9 ;"
BMOV_B_L: FIXED  # e.g. "BMOV.32 B15, MACTIVE ;"
BMOV_B_R: FIXED  # e.g. "BMOV.32 B6, R16 ;"
BMOV_L_B: FIXED  # e.g. "BMOV.32.PQUAD MACTIVE, B15 ;"
BMOV_R_B: FIXED  # e.g. "BMOV.32.CLEAR R16, B6 ;"
BPT_II: FIXED  # e.g. "BPT.TRAP 0x1 ;"
BRA_II: FIXED  # e.g. "BRA 0x110;"
BRA_P_II: FIXED  # e.g. "@!P1 BRA !P2, 0x7f0 ;"
BRA_UR_II: FIXED  # e.g. "BRA.DIV ~URZ, 0x3910 ;"
BREAK_B: FIXED  # e.g. "@!P0 BREAK B0 ;"
BREAK_P_B: FIXED  # e.g. "@!P0 BREAK P2, B2 ;"
BRXU_UR_II: FIXED  # e.g. "BRXU UR18 -0x7360 ;"
BRX_R_II: FIXED  # e.g. "BRX R14 -0x390 ;"
BSSY_B_II: FIXED  # e.g. "BSSY B0, 0x940 ;"
BSYNC_B: FIXED  # e.g. "BSYNC B1 ;"
CALL_II: FIXED  # e.g. "CALL.REL.NOINC 0x200 ;"
CALL_R: FIXED  # e.g. "CALL.ABS.NOINC R12 ;"
CALL_R_II: FIXED  # e.g. "CALL.REL.NOINC R8 0x0 ;"
DEPBAR_SB_II: FIXED  # consumes/waits on an existing barrier, doesn't set one  # e.g. "DEPBAR.LE SB0, 0x1 ;"
DEPBAR_SB_II_SBSET: FIXED  # e.g. "DEPBAR.LE SB0, 0x0, {4,3,2,1} ;"
ERRBAR: FIXED  # e.g. "ERRBAR;"
EXIT: FIXED  # e.g. "@P0 EXIT ;"
EXIT_P: FIXED  # e.g. "@!P0 EXIT P1 ;"
LEPC_R: FIXED  # writes a deterministic PC value, not memory/SFU-pipe data  # e.g. "LEPC R32 ;"
MEMBAR: FIXED  # e.g. "MEMBAR.SC.CTA ;"
NANOSLEEP_II: FIXED  # e.g. "NANOSLEEP 0xf4240 ;"
NANOSLEEP_R: FIXED  # e.g. "NANOSLEEP R0 ;"
NOP: FIXED  # e.g. "NOP;"
RET_R_II: FIXED  # e.g. "RET.REL.NODEC R2 0x0 ;"
WARPSYNC_II: FIXED  # e.g. "WARPSYNC 0xffffffff ;"
WARPSYNC_R: FIXED  # e.g. "WARPSYNC R0 ;"
YIELD: FIXED  # e.g. "YIELD ;"

# ==== Unbucketed: 4 curated ====
#
# HMNMX2 (half2 min/max with predicate select) is structurally identical to the already-confirmed
# FMNMX/IMNMX (FIXED, fast ALU pipe) -- just a different operand width, not a different pipe.
# LDGDEPBAR is the async-copy analogue of DEPBAR: it waits on/consumes an existing async-copy
# barrier rather than setting one (FIXED, same reasoning). ARRIVES_AURI has an address operand but
# no destination register at all -- no operand for a scoreboard barrier to protect (FIXED, same
# mechanical reasoning as CCTL_ARI). See Reports/tasks.md Phase 1.1.

ARRIVES_AURI: FIXED  # e.g. "@!P1 ARRIVES.LDGSTSBAR.64 [UR4] ;"
HMNMX2_R_R_R_P: FIXED  # e.g. "HMNMX2 R43, R4, R82.H0_H0, !PT ;"
HMNMX2_R_R_cAI_P: FIXED  # e.g. "HMNMX2 R43, R4, c[0x0] [0x298].H0_H0, !PT ;"
LDGDEPBAR: FIXED  # e.g. "LDGDEPBAR ;"
